newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: UNHCR puts on hold most programmes in Kabul.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR puts on hold most programmes in Kabul.

text.p: The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said on Wednesday it was putting most of its activities in Kabul on hold because of arrests and intimidation of its staff by the Taleban militia.
"We are putting on hold most of our programmes in Kabul until the security situation improves," Rupert Colville, a spokesman for the UNHCR, said.

He said four of the 22 local staff in the UNHCR's main office in Kabul had been arrested, while seven Afghan women employees had been told to stay at home since the Taleban militia captured Kabul on September 27.
"We are extremely concerned about the safety of our four arrested staffers, one of whom has been missing for nearly four weeks," Colville said. "The rest of the staff are petrified."
The virtual suspension of UNHCR activities coincides with the start of a vital winter relief programme for Kabul.

The agency says that effective security guarantees are lacking, despite assurances given by the Taleban authorities. Other international relief agencies and news organisations operating in Kabul say their local staff have also faced increasing harrassment by the Taleban in recent weeks.
